category: E · Domain, interface, and temporal decomposition

formulations.name: Local subdomain PINNs
formulations.category: E · Domain, interface, and temporal decomposition
formulations.meaning: Assigns separate trainable approximations to spatial subdomains.
formulations.purpose: Localizes representation and optimization in large or heterogeneous domains.
formulations.relation: It replaces one global trial function by coupled local trial functions.
formulations.symbols: \(\Omega_k\): subdomain; \(K\): number of subdomains; \(\theta_k\): local parameters.

formulations.name: Subdomain state coupling
formulations.category: E · Domain, interface, and temporal decomposition
formulations.meaning: Requires local subnetworks to agree on a shared interface when the state is continuous.
formulations.purpose: Reconstructs a coherent global field from local models.
formulations.relation: It is the interface constraint associated with spatial decomposition.

formulations.name: Conservative subdomain flux coupling
formulations.category: E · Domain, interface, and temporal decomposition
formulations.meaning: Balances oriented fluxes across a shared subdomain interface.
formulations.purpose: Preserves conservative transmission between locally trained models.
formulations.relation: It strengthens simple state continuity with a physically integral coupling condition.

formulations.name: Domain-decomposed composite objective
formulations.category: E · Domain, interface, and temporal decomposition
formulations.meaning: Aggregates local residual objectives and interface coupling terms.
formulations.purpose: Defines the optimization problem of a decomposed PINN.
formulations.relation: It shows that decomposition changes both architecture and loss construction.

formulations.name: Gated soft decomposition
formulations.category: E · Domain, interface, and temporal decomposition
formulations.meaning: Combines expert subnetworks through a trainable gating function rather than a hard spatial partition.
formulations.purpose: Provides soft specialization across the domain.
formulations.relation: It is the defining mixture structure of gating-based soft decomposition.

formulations.name: Progressive residual-driven decomposition
formulations.category: E · Domain, interface, and temporal decomposition
formulations.meaning: Uses the residual averaged over the actual sampling distribution of each subdomain to identify poorly learned regions for further decomposition or retraining.
formulations.purpose: Concentrates model capacity where the current approximation is weakest.
formulations.relation: The sampling measure is made explicit so the expectation is well defined for space-time training rather than incorrectly treating the full input descriptor as an element of a purely spatial set.
formulations.symbols: \(k^\star\): selected difficult subdomain; \(\mathcal P_k\): sampling distribution supported on subdomain \(\Omega_k\) and its training-time interval.

formulations.name: Parallel block-gradient objective aggregation
formulations.category: E · Domain, interface, and temporal decomposition
formulations.meaning: Writes the distributed objective as a sum of local losses plus an interface coupling term, with one gradient equation for each local parameter block.
formulations.purpose: Expresses parallel/local optimization without incorrectly adding gradients that live in different parameter spaces.
formulations.relation: Local residual work can be evaluated in parallel, while interface terms couple the parameter blocks and require the corresponding interface-gradient contribution for each subdomain.
formulations.symbols: \(\theta_k\): parameter block of subdomain \(k\); \(\mathcal{L}^{(k)}\): local objective; \(\mathcal{L}_{IF}\): interface-coupling objective.

formulations.name: Temporal-window decomposition
formulations.category: E · Domain, interface, and temporal decomposition
formulations.meaning: Partitions a long time horizon into trainable windows.
formulations.purpose: Reduces the difficulty of learning long-time dynamics globally.
formulations.relation: It applies decomposition to time rather than space.

formulations.name: Time-marching state transfer
formulations.category: E · Domain, interface, and temporal decomposition
formulations.meaning: Transfers the terminal state of one time block to initialize or constrain the next.
formulations.relation: It replaces one global-in-time solve by linked local-in-time solves.

formulations.name: Sequential time-block objective
formulations.category: E · Domain, interface, and temporal decomposition
formulations.meaning: Trains each temporal block conditional on the converged state from the preceding block.
formulations.relation: It is a sequential alternative to simultaneous residual minimization over the entire time interval.

formulations.name: One-network-per-region/phase representation
formulations.category: E · Domain, interface, and temporal decomposition
formulations.meaning: Assigns separate subnetworks to material regions, phases, fractures, or physical constituents.
formulations.relation: It couples architecture directly to the physical partition of the problem.

formulations.name: Shared-trunk / branched physical outputs
formulations.category: E · Domain, interface, and temporal decomposition
formulations.meaning: Uses shared latent features followed by field- or task-specific branches.
formulations.purpose: Captures common physical structure while preserving specialized outputs.
formulations.relation: It is useful when coupled states share information but have distinct residuals or measurements.

formulations.name: Space–time decomposition
formulations.category: E · Domain, interface, and temporal decomposition
formulations.meaning: Partitions the combined space-time domain into local problems.
formulations.purpose: Supports local specialization in both geometry and temporal evolution.
formulations.relation: It generalizes purely spatial and purely temporal decomposition.
